sentences.text: Today we will talk about Oman.
Oman is a peaceful and beautiful country in the Middle East.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Oman?
Oman is in western Asia on the southeast corner of the Arabian Peninsula.
It is next to Saudi Arabia, Yemen, and the United Arab Emirates.
To the east, Oman touches the Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Oman.
Oman has deserts, mountains, and a long coastline.
What is the capital city of Oman?
The capital city is Muscat.
Muscat is next to the sea.
It is clean, quiet, and full of history.
In Muscat, you can see mosques, traditional markets, suks, palaces, modern buildings.
Other cities in Oman include Salala, Nizwa, and Sohar.
How many people live in Oman?
About 4.5 million people live in Oman.
Many people are Omani, but there are also workers from other countries.
Most people live in cities and towns near the coast.
What language do people speak in Oman?
The official language is Arabic.
People speak modern standard Arabic and Omani Arabic.
Many people also speak English, especially in schools, shops, and offices.
Some people speak Swahili, Baluchi, or Hindi too.
Oman is a multilingual country.
What is the weather like in Oman?
Oman is a hot and dry country.
Most of the year, the weather is very hot, especially in summer.
In the desert, it can be over 45 degrees threes in the day.
At night, it gets cooler.
In Salala in the south, there is a special season called Karif.
It brings rain and green hills in the summer months.
What does Oman look like?
Oman has many kinds of land.
Sandy deserts with dunes, rocky mountains like Jabal Shams, waddies, dry riverbeds with water in the rainy season, beaches and coastal towns.
The country is clean, calm, and very natural.
People care about nature and tradition.
What animals live in Oman?
In Oman, you can find camels, goats and sheep, donkeys, foxes, hyenas, and wild cats in the mountains, turtles and dolphins near the coast.
You can also see falcons and eagles in the sky.
In the desert, there are many lizards, snakes, and insects.
What do people eat in Oman?
Omani food is simple, fresh, and flavorful.
People eat rice, grilled meat or chicken, fish flatbread, dates and fruit.
Popular dishes include shuwa, slow -cooked lamb and a fire pit, moj boos, spiced rice with meat or fish, haris, wheat and meat cooked together, halwa, a sweet dessert made with sugar and nuts.
People often eat together, sitting on the floor and share the food.
What do people drink in Oman?
People drink Karak tea, black tea with milk and spices.
Arabic coffee, kahwa with cardamom, often served with dates, water, juices made from mango, lemon or banana.
Coffee and dates are important in Omani hospitality.
Guests are always offered a drink and a smile.
What is life like in Oman?
Life in Oman is peaceful, respectful and family -centered.
People go to school, work and spend time with family.
On weekends, people visit the mountains, beaches or villages.
Omani people enjoy picnics in nature, driving in the desert, going to the souk market, reading, cooking and talking with family.
Traditional clothing is common.
Men wear a dish dasha, long robe, and women wear colorful abayas and scarves.
What are some holidays and traditions in Oman?
Eat Al -Feeder after Ramadan with big family meals.
Eat Al -Adha with prayers and meat sharing.
National Day November 18th with parades and flags.
Ramadan a holy month of fasting and prayer.
Omanis love poetry, music and traditional dance.
At weddings and festivals, people sing and play drums.
Some fun facts about Oman.
Oman has no skyscrapers.
Buildings are low and traditional.
Camels are important and sometimes used in races.
Frankincense, used in perfume, comes from Omani trees.
Oman is one of the safest countries in the world.
The Omani flag is red, white and green with a small symbol, two swords and a dagger.
Now you know many things about Oman.
You know where it is, what people speak, and how they live.
You learned about the food, weather, animals and traditions.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
